answer: My answer to sybils is Zero-knowledge proof the text came from a live human session — a proof the keystrokes came from a live session — which makes the spiral of cheating a bill the attacker pays again for every clone. The check runs before any reward is issued, so a sybil earns nothing for trying; the reef is that the attacker discovers the price before the first coin, not after. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the sable of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
